0.body: Synechocystis is a cyanobacterium with no nucleus. It lives on light: oxygenic photosynthesis on membranes, no chloroplasts. Lab model for hydrogen metabolism.

1.body: Anabaena variabilis is a filament. Some cells become heterocysts and fix nitrogen while neighbours make sugar. In the pond it supplies bound nitrogen.

2.body: Spirulina (Arthrospira) is a coil of cells with gas vesicles. It hangs near the surface, photosynthesizes, and is edible. In-game it is a large green screw at the water film.

3.body: Nostoc punctiforme is a bead chain in a slime capsule. It lives free or in plant symbiosis. The colony looks like a clump of green beads.

4.body: Oscillatoria limnetica is a gliding filament. It oscillates side to side and can photosynthesize without releasing oxygen. Typical of silt and surface film.

5.body: Microcystis aeruginosa is a mucilage colony, often toxic (microcystin). It causes water bloom. In-game it is a green colony ball, risky prey.

6.body: Gloeocapsa is paired cells in colored sheaths. It lives on rocks and soil and tolerates UV. In the pond it is small paired cocci in a coat.

7.body: Lyngbya majuscula is a thick cyanobacterial filament. It can release irritating toxins. It forms mats near warm shores.

8.body: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is a green cell with two flagella and an eyespot. It swims toward light. Classic algal genetics model.

9.body: Chlorella vulgaris is a non-motile green ball. It divides fast and is protein-rich. Food for small eaters and a space-food subject.

10.body: Volvox globator is a hollow sphere of thousands of cells. Daughter colonies ripen inside and exit. In-game it is a large green colony.

11.body: Euglena gracilis is a mixotroph: chloroplasts plus the ability to eat. A red eyespot tracks light. Green by day; in the dark it switches to food.

12.body: Scenedesmus quadricauda is usually four cells in a row with end spines. Spines make swallowing harder. It does not swim — it drifts.

13.body: Haematococcus pluvialis is a green motile cell; under stress it turns red (astaxanthin) and grows a thick wall. Red cysts survive drought.

14.body: Dunaliella salina has no rigid wall and lives in very salty water. It stores beta-carotene and looks orange. Two flagella.

15.body: Micrasterias rotata is a flat star desmid. Two mirrored halves with deep cuts. Non-motile; photosynthesizes in acidic bog water.

16.body: Navicula is a boat-shaped diatom with a silica valve. It glides on the substrate along a raphe slit. The shell remains after death.

17.body: Pinnularia viridis is a large pennate diatom. Silica shell with a symmetric pattern. It glides slowly on the bottom.

18.body: Cyclotella meneghiniana is a circular centric diatom. It floats as a disc; the shell is two lids. Typical plankton.

19.body: Diatoma vulgare is a diatom that sticks into a zigzag. The colony increases drag in the water column.

20.body: Rhodospirillum rubrum is a purple spiral. Anoxygenic photosynthesis plus organics. Red color comes from bacteriochlorophyll.

21.body: Chromatium vinosum is a purple sulfur bacterium. It oxidizes hydrogen sulfide and stores sulfur granules. Lives at the oxygen/sulfur boundary.

22.body: Porphyridium cruentum is a unicellular red alga. Phycoerythrin gives a blood-red color. Mucilage coat, no flagella.

23.body: Prochlorococcus marinus is the smallest and most abundant photosynthetic cell on Earth. Discovered in the 1980s. It feeds the ocean.

24.body: Chroococcidiopsis thermalis is an extremophile: desert, rock, radiation. A candidate for life beyond Earth. In the pond it is a slow coccus colony.

25.body: Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus is a tiny bacterial predator. It screws into another cell and multiplies until the host bursts.

26.body: Vampirococcus sits on prey from the outside and sucks out the contents without entering. A bacterial vampire.

27.body: Daptobacter enters a prey bacterium and eats it from inside. A rare intracellular hunter.

28.body: Myxococcus xanthus is a social bacterium. In a pack it surrounds prey and releases enzymes. When starved it forms a fruiting body.

29.body: Bacteriovorax stolpii is a marine Bdellovibrio relative. It attacks Gram-negatives and lives in the prey periplasm.

30.body: Halobacteriovorax is a salt-tolerant bacterial hunter. Same trick: puncture the wall and grow inside.

31.body: Peredibacter starrii is another BALO predator. A fast comma-shaped flagellate targeting large rods.

32.body: Monas guttula is a small heterotrophic flagellate. It grabs bacteria at the detritus surface.

33.body: Oikomonas termo is a drop-shaped flagellate. One flagellum; it hunts in bacterial film.

34.body: Anthophysa vegetans is a colony on an iron-manganese stalk. Cells sit in a tuft and catch bacteria.

35.body: Chilomonas paramecium is a colorless cryptophyte. Two flagella; it eats dissolved organics and tiny bacteria, no chloroplasts.

36.body: Cercomonas longicauda is an amoeboflagellate with a long tail. It crawls and swallows bacteria with pseudopodia.

37.body: Heteromita globosa is a soil flagellate. Two flagella of different length; a main bacterial eater in soil.

38.body: Bodo saltans is a kinetoplastid. It 'dances' in place, attached by the rear flagellum, and snatches bacteria.

39.body: Procryptobia sorokini is a Bodo relative. It swims freely and strikes prey with the anterior flagellum.

40.body: Trypanosoma brucei is a blood parasite causing sleeping sickness. Undulating membrane and one flagellum. In the pond it is a slim-hunter model.

41.body: Leishmania donovani is an intracellular human parasite. Flagellated in the insect, aflagellate inside a macrophage.

42.body: Monosiga brevicollis is a choanoflagellate, an animal relative. A microvilli collar filters bacteria.

43.body: Salpingoeca rosetta is a sessile choanoflagellate in a lorica. It can form a rosette. It filters a water current.

44.body: Codonosiga botrytis is a choanoflagellate colony on a shared stalk. Several filters on one stem.

45.body: Paramecium caudatum is the classic slipper. Thousands of cilia, an oral groove, contractile vacuoles. It filters bacteria.

46.body: Paramecium bursaria is a slipper with zoochlorella symbionts. Green inside: sugar from algae by day, filtering at night.

47.body: Stentor coeruleus is a blue trumpet up to a millimetre. It flares into a funnel and drives a current with cilia. It can swim or sit.

48.body: Stentor polymorphus is a relative of the blue stentor, often with zoochlorellae. Shape shifts from trumpet to ball.

49.body: Vorticella campanula is a bell on a contractile stalk. The stalk coils into a spiral instantly. The cell itself does not swim away.

50.body: Vorticella microstoma is a small bell. Same spring-stalk, a narrower oral field. Often on detritus.

51.body: Didinium nasutum is a barrel hunter of slippers. It fires toxicysts and swallows prey whole, even if the prey is larger.

52.body: Spirostomum ambiguum is a very long cigar. It contracts several-fold in a fraction of a second. Cilia run in a spiral.

53.body: Blepharisma americanum is a pink ciliate. Blepharismin pigment is light-sensitive. It filters and can attack smaller cells.

54.body: Euplotes patella walks on cirri as if on legs. Flat, quick turns. It scrapes bacteria off surfaces.

55.body: Stylonychia pustulata is a hypotrich that 'runs' on the bottom. Large cirri, a clear mouth. Predator of small ciliates.

56.body: Oxytricha trifallax is a genome model: two nuclei and complex DNA rewriting. It walks on cirri and eats bacteria and small protists.

57.body: Tetrahymena thermophila is a lab ciliate. Four oral membranelles, fast division. Model for telomeres and cilia.

58.body: Coleps hirtus is a barrel in calcareous plates with spines. Scavenger and predator: it bites into the wounded.

59.body: Litonotus lamella is a flat predator with toxicysts in a 'proboscis'. It paralyzes prey and sucks it out.

60.body: Dileptus anser has a long neck with venomous extrusomes. It strikes with the neck, then swallows. A large mid-tier hunter.

61.body: Urocentrum turbo is a spinning top: an equatorial ciliary belt spins the cell in place. It filters bacteria.

62.body: Zoothamnium arbuscula is a branched colony of bells. A shared contractile stalk jerks the whole tree at once.

63.body: Opercularia coarctata is a sessile peritrich without a spring stalk. A lid covers the mouth. It filters and does not swim away.

64.body: Amoeba proteus is the classic amoeba. Pseudopodia flow around prey. No fixed shape, no cilia.

65.body: Arcella vulgaris is a testate amoeba with a rigid dome. Pseudopodia emerge from the aperture. It crawls on plants.

66.body: Difflugia oblonga has a shell of sand grains the amoeba glues itself. It lives in silt.

67.body: Euglypha alveolata has a shell of silica scales. Thin filose pseudopodia. A small bacterial predator.

68.body: Nebela collaris is a bottle-shaped shell built from stolen scales. Forest and bog waters.

69.body: Centropyxis aculeata is a disc shell with spines. The aperture is offset. It crawls on detritus.

70.body: Actinophrys sol is a heliozoan: thin axopodia radiate all around. Prey sticks to the rays and is pulled in.

71.body: Actinosphaerium eichhorni is a large multinucleate heliozoan. Same rays, much bigger cell. It eats ciliates and rotifers.

72.body: Raphidiophrys pallida is a heliozoan in scales. Rays carry silica needles. An ambush plankton hunter.

73.body: Rotaria rotatoria is a rotifer that can survive drying. A corona wheels food into the mouth. A true multicellular animal.

74.body: Philodina roseola is a pink bdelloid rotifer. It crawls like a leech and also swims. Females only; no males.

75.body: Brachionus plicatilis is a planktonic loricate rotifer. Fry food in aquaculture. It filters algae and bacteria.

76.body: Keratella cochlearis is a rotifer with a long lorica spine. The spine deters predators. Common pond plankton.

77.body: Asplanchna priodonta is a sack without a lorica, a predatory rotifer. It swallows other rotifers and ciliates whole.

78.body: Chaetonotus maximus is a gastrotrich. Scale-covered, it crawls on the bottom. It eats bacteria and detritus.

79.body: Lepidodermella squamata is a small gastrotrich in overlapping scales. Very fast in-place turns.

80.body: Macrostomum lignano is a microscopic flatworm. Real muscles and eyes. A regeneration model. It hunts small protists.

81.body: Stenostomum leucops is a thin ciliated worm. It divides across into a chain of zooids. Predator of detritus and small animals.

82.body: Microstomum lineare is a flatworm that eats hydra and embeds their stinging cells in its own skin. A chain of zooids.

83.body: Prostoma graecense is a freshwater nemertean. A long proboscis shoots at prey. A rare large bottom hunter.

84.body: Trichoplax adhaerens is a placozoan, among the simplest animals. It crawls as a sheet and digests food outside. No mouth.

85.body: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is baker's yeast. It buds, eats sugar, releases CO2 and alcohol. In the pond it cleans dissolved organics.

86.body: Candida albicans is a yeast that can grow as filaments. An opportunistic human pathogen. In-game it is a detrital fungus.

87.body: Mucor mucedo is bread mold. Sporangia on stalks, fast growth over the dead. It does not hunt the living.

88.body: Rhizopus stolonifer is black bread mold. Stolons and rhizoids spread over the substrate. It breaks down starch.

89.body: Penicillium chrysogenum is a brush mold, the source of penicillin. Conidial brushes. It decomposes organics and suppresses nearby bacteria.

90.body: Aspergillus niger is black aspergillus. Spherical spore heads. Industrial citric-acid producer. A saprotroph.

91.body: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis is a chytrid of frogs. Uniflagellate zoospores. In the pond it is a water-fungus model.

92.body: Chytriomyces aureus is a water chytrid on pollen and algae. Golden sporangia; zoospores swim to the substrate.

93.body: Allomyces macrogynus is a water fungus with true mycelium. It alternates diploid and haploid. Zoospores have a posterior flagellum.

94.body: Bacillus subtilis is a soil rod. Spores survive boiling. It breaks down protein; a Gram-positive model.

95.body: Pseudomonas putida is a cleanup rod. It even eats petroleum products. Motile flagellum, fast growth on detritus.

96.body: Streptomyces coelicolor is a filamentous soil bacterium. It makes the smell of earth (geosmin) and many antibiotics. Spores on hyphae.

97.body: Cellulomonas fimi breaks down cellulose. A yellow rod on plant detritus. Without it dead algae would linger longer.

98.body: Thermus aquaticus is a thermophile from hot springs. Taq polymerase is the basis of PCR. In a cold pond it is almost dormant.

99.body: Deinococcus radiodurans is the radiation champion. It reassembles a shattered genome in hours. Thick wall, cell tetrads.

1001.body: Sexual Eukaryote is a teaching model of sexual reproduction. Two sexes, gamete fusion, not simple binary fission.

T4 Bacteriophage.body: T4 is a large myovirus of E. coli. The tail contracts and injects DNA. In half an hour the cell bursts and dozens of phages exit.

Lambda Phage.body: Lambda is a temperate phage. It can insert into the chromosome and sleep (lysogeny) or cut the cell at once (lysis).

T7 Bacteriophage.body: T7 has a short tail and very fast replication. A favourite system in synthetic biology.

Phi-6 Phage.body: Phi-6 is an RNA phage with a lipid envelope. It infects Pseudomonas. A rare membrane for a phage.

MS2 Phage.body: MS2 is a tiny tailless RNA phage. It binds male E. coli pili. Its genome was one of the first RNA genomes read.

Neuro-Parasite.body: A fictional pond neuro-parasite. It latches onto eukaryotes and breaks host behaviour until the host becomes a carrier.

Sexual Eukaryote.body: Sexual Eukaryote is a teaching model of sexual reproduction. Two sexes, gamete fusion, not simple binary fission.
